html:
At Stiklestad, on 29 July 1030, King Olaf Haraldsson was killed fighting farmers and chieftains backed by Cnut the Great. Within a year he was hailed as a saint.

Olaf had ruled Norway from 1015 and forced Christianity on it, often by violence. His enemies drove him into exile, and he died trying to win back his throne. Soon stories of miracles spread, his body was found not to have decayed, and he was declared a saint in 1031.

Saint Olaf, the eternal king of Norway, became the centre of a national church. Pilgrims came from all over the north to his shrine at Nidaros in Trondheim. His death completed the conversion of Norway, and 29 July is still Olsok, his feast day.
